newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo head says privatisation is historic move.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo head says privatisation is historic move.

text.p: Italy's largest bank, Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino, needs to diversify its activities and boost efficiency in order to secure a prosperous future after it is privatised, chairman Gianni Zandano said.

Speaking at the bank's annual shareholders meeting in Turin Zandano said "merely bearing down on operating costs risks being insufficient to make up the income gap that Italian banks face in comparison with banks in other systems."
Zandano said San Paolo, which is in the process of being privatised, needed to boost operating profits.

San Paolo's cost to income ratio stood at 75 percent, far higher than British banks at 62 percent and German banks at 67 percent, but better than French banks which had an 80 percent ratio, said Zandano.
"San Paolo's objective can only be to reduce the cost/income ratio," said Zandano, adding that high operating and personnel costs were "an element of weakness in the Italian banking system."

He said the bank had to pursue a strategy of diversification by moving into asset management, corporate finance and handling of payments systems while gaining a presence in overseas countries with fast-growing economies.
The bank also had to increase its points of contact with the client base "by taking advantage of all the opportunities put at its disposal by technology aand marketing."
"San Paolo's strategy, aimed at achieving a significant increase in Return on Equity (ROE), must move on different fronts," he said.

The bank's managing director Dario Pasqua, who later announced his resignation, said ROE had risen to 6.1 percent in 1996 from 4.6 percent the previous year, adding: "This represents only a first step towards levels of profitability which are competitive with those of the main European financial institutions."

San Paolo is going ahead on May 19 with a public share offer of 25 percent of the bank's stock after privately placing 20 percent with friendly banks and financial institutions who together will form a core of stable shareholders.

The entities which are party to the stability pact are IFI and IFIL (five percent of voting rights), IMI (five percent), Banco Santander (five percent), San Paolo Bank Holding (five percent), Monte dei Paschi di Siena (three percent), Reale Mutua Assicurazioni (three percent) and Kredietbank (two percent).
San Paolo Holding is the holding company through which Compagnia di San Paolo, a foundation, has exercised control of the bank.
Following the private placement, San Paolo's stake in the bank has fallen to 45.6 percent from 65.6 percent and will fall further to around 20 percent on completion of the public share offering.
Under the stability pact, San Paolo Holding will only be recognised as holding five percent of the bank's stock for the purpose of exercising voting rights.
